writeup:
SCOPE: Verified items (1),(2),(3) of the Koszul-descent no-go by exact rational arithmetic. Code at /home/user/multi-agent-environment/.claude/worktrees/wf_a939e8f4-f79-3/audit_koszul/verify.py builds Lambda^* V explicitly (V=Std_p realized via basis b_k=e_k-e_{p-1}, Gram = I+J), forms the wedge operator d_i and interior-product operator h_i as 2^(p-1) x 2^(p-1) rational matrices, and also runs brute-force class-function checks over the full symmetric group. All results are exact (Fraction), not floating point.

ITEM (1) — HOMOTOPY IDENTITY. For every root i in 0..p-1 and both p=5,7, h_i d_i + d_i h_i = id EXACTLY on all of Lambda^* V (16-dim for p=5, 64-dim for p=7). Also phi_i(v_i)=1 exactly. This is CONFIRMED and is in fact a special case of the universal antiderivation identity iota_phi(v ^ w) + v ^ iota_phi(w) = phi(v)*w, which collapses to id precisely because phi_i(v_i)=(p/(p-1))*<v_i,v_i>=(p/(p-1))*((p-1)/p)=1. RKD.1 (contractibility of the tautological Koszul complex on the root cover, equivalently lambda_{-1}(V)|_{S_{p-1}}=0 realized by an acyclic Koszul complex on the nonzero H_i-fixed vector v_i) is therefore an exact, standard theorem. VERDICT: CONFIRMED.

ITEM (2) — DESCENT FAILURE. v_j - v_i = e_j - e_i exactly (confirmed for pairs (0,1),(0,2),(1,2)), with ||v_j-v_i||^2 = 2 exactly, hence nowhere zero on the ordered-distinct-root component. As operators on Lambda^* V, d_i - d_j != 0 and h_i - h_j != 0 (both nonzero at p=5,7). So the two root-selected contractions really do disagree, and the mismatch cocycle is a nonzero section over the off-diagonal component of X x_U X, which is finite etale and dominant over the generic t-line (away from t=+/-1,infinity and the q-boundaries). A boundary-supported correction cannot cancel a section that is generically nonzero on a dominant component. RKD.2 is CONFIRMED. ONE PRECISION NOTE: item (2) on its own proves only that the SPECIFIC tautological/root-selected homotopy does not glue and cannot be boundary-corrected; it does not by itself prove that NO descent whatsoever exists. The universal "no boundary-supported or O(p) correction" statement is carried by RKD.3/RKD.4 (below), which the doc does supply — so there is no net overclaim, but the Cech-cocycle computation should not be read as the decisive no-go by itself.

ITEM (3) — CONCEPTUAL / RESTRICTION CLAIM. Brute force over all p! permutations at p=5 and p=7: char(Lambda_p)(g)=det(I-g|V) = p exactly when g is a single p-cycle and 0 for every other permutation. (Reason: det(I-g|P)=0 always since 1vec is fixed; on V one trivial eigenvalue is removed, so det(I-g|V) still contains a factor (1-1)=0 unless g has a single cycle, i.e. is a p-cycle, in which case it equals prod_{zeta^p=1,zeta!=1}(1-zeta)=p.) Thus (1/p)*char(Lambda_p) IS the p-cycle indicator. Restricted to S_{p-1}=Stab(root), which contains no p-cycle, char(Lambda_p) is identically 0 (confirmed: every element fixing the last point evaluates to 0). So selecting a root (restricting to S_{p-1}) sends the p-cycle class — and every derangement class — to zero. WHAT THIS PROVES: the root cover trivializes the alternating hook object precisely on the fixed-point-free Frobenius sector that carries the entire arithmetic content (irreducible degree-p fibres <=> Frobenius = p-cycle). The contraction is exact exactly where the target indicator is invisible. This is an exact identity, not a heuristic, so RKD.5's conceptual no-go ("the obstruction is the global fixed-point-free Frobenius sector, not a boundary defect") is CONFIRMED as a correct statement about the mechanism. It does NOT, and does not purport to, prove the crown; it explains WHY root-selection cannot reach it.

RULING ON THE NO-GO (does it establish "no boundary-supported or O(p)-rank descent correction", or only make it plausible?): ESTABLISHED within its stated scope. The decisive, load-bearing result is RKD.4: since Lambda^i V = S^{(p-i,1^i)} are pairwise non-isomorphic hook irreducibles (distinct partitions) each entering Lambda_p with coefficient (-1)^i, uniqueness of irreducible character expansion forces any effective presentation Lambda_p=[A]-[B] by honest local systems to satisfy dim A,dim B >= sum_{i even}C(p-1,i)=2^(p-2) and total rank >= 2^(p-1). I confirmed 2^(p-1) = 16, 64, 1024, 4096 for p=5,7,11,13 with even/odd binomial sums each exactly 2^(p-2). An O(p) generic correction is exponentially smaller than this floor, so it is genuinely refuted, not merely made implausible. Any actual complex of local systems on U representing the alternating sum has honest graded pieces, so the bound applies to real geometric objects (not just virtual ones), closing the obvious escape. RKD.3 (Hom_G(K_even,K_odd)=0 because the hooks are distinct irreducibles) correctly rules out a generic G-equivariant parity-reversing differential on the same graded object. IMPORTANT CORRECT SCOPING: this no-go concerns the PRE-pushforward, generic/root-cover object only. It does not touch — and the doc explicitly leaves open (section 8) — cancellation of common semisimple constituents AFTER the fixed-q H^1_c pushforward and semisimplification on the q-line, where cohomology groups (not the graded hook local systems) can cancel common Frobenius factors and potentially leave O(p) unmatched rank. That surviving statement is a different object; RKD.4 neither proves nor refutes it, and the doc does not claim otherwise. CONCLUSION: The Koszul-descent no-go is honestly stated and internally sound; its four exact theorems (RKD.1-2 verified by direct computation, RKD.3-4-5 by exact representation theory / exhaustive class-function evaluation) hold. No overclaim of the crown is present. The only refinement worth flagging is that the strength of the no-go rests on RKD.4's exponential rank floor, with item (2)'s cocycle computation being necessary context but not, by itself, sufficient for the universal statement.

Confirmed 2^(p-2) even = 2^(p-2) odd for p=5,7,11,13; total 2^(p-1)=16,64,1024,4096. Applies to honest (non-virtual) local systems, so the bound is geometric. O(p) << 2^(p-1): genuinely refuted.
